questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Silica is a network solid with $\mathrm{Si}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{Si}$ bonds. In many aluminosilicates, a few Si atoms in the silica structure are replaced by Al atoms. Zeolites, clays, asbestos etc. are examples of aluminosilicates having different structures. The statement which is NOT correct is:
options: The basic structural unit in silicates is tetrahedral $\left(\mathrm{SiO}_4\right)^{4-}$.
Replacement of a Si atom in silica by an Al atom results in negative charge on the Al atom.
Silica dissolves in aqueous NaOH to form sodium silicate in which $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ is bonded to oxyanions.
Silicones are examples of silicates.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Lewis acidity of boron halides follow the order (\approx$ meaning approximately equal to)$
options: $\mathrm{BF}_3 \approx \mathrm{BBr}_3 \approx \mathrm{BCl}_3$
$\mathrm{BF}_3 < \mathrm{BCl}_3 < \mathrm{BBr}_3$
$\mathrm{BCl}_3 \approx \mathrm{BBr}_3 < \mathrm{BF}_3$
$\mathrm{BBr}_3 < \mathrm{BCl}_3 < \mathrm{BF}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Boron on reaction with fluorine forms $\mathbf{P}$, which on reaction with NaH at a high temperature produces $\mathbf{Q}$ along with a sodium salt. $\mathbf{P}$ on reaction with $\mathrm{NH}_3$ in $1: 1$ ratio gives $\mathbf{R}$. $\mathbf{Q}$ on reaction with $\mathrm{NH}_3$ in $1: 2$ ratio at an elevated temperature gives S. The correct statement is
options: $\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{N}$ bond in $\mathbf{R}$ is covalent in nature.
$\mathrm{All}\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds in $\mathbf{Q}$ are equivalent.
The shape of $\mathbf{S}$ is tetrahedral.
Compound $\mathbf{Q}$ when dissolved in water gives an acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxidation of sodium borohydride with iodine forms a colourless toxic gas $\mathbf{X}$ which catches fire spontaneously on exposure to air. $\mathbf{X}$ undergoes hydrolysis to yield a white crystalline solid $\mathbf{Y}$. The correct statement(s) about $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ is/are
options: The oxidation state of the central atom in $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ is +3.
The compound $\mathbf{X}$ has both terminal and bridging hydrogens.
The compound $\mathbf{Y}$ forms a layered type structure through hydrogen bonding interaction.
The compound $\mathbf{X}$ reacts with ammonia to form benzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Boron and nitrogen form bonds analogous to carbon-carbon bonds. For example, compound ammonia borane, $\mathrm{NH}_3-\mathrm{BH}_3$, contains $\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{N}$ bond analogous to the $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}$ bond in ethane. Borazine $\left(\mathrm{B}_3 \mathrm{~N}_3 \mathrm{H}_6\right)$ is analogous to benzene and is prepared by reacting $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$ with $\mathrm{BCl}_3$ followed by reduction using $\mathrm{LiBH}_4$. The correct statement(s) is/are
options: Boron nitride (BN) has a structure similar to graphite and is a good conductor of electricity.
The B-center in borazine is susceptible to nucleophilic attack.
Ethane is a gas at room temperature, while ammonia borane is not so.
The reaction of HCl with borazine gives hexachloro derivative of borazine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reaction of methyl chloride with silicon at 573 K in the presence of copper as a catalyst produces substitued chlorosilanes. Hydrolysis of chlorosilanes produces silanols. The silanols with appropriate substitution, thus formed, are used to make silicone polymers. The correct statement in this context is:
options: Only two different chlorosilanes are produced in the reaction of methyl chloride with silicon.
A silicate is formed on condensation polymerization of silanols.
The chain length of the silcone polymer can be controlled by adding trimethylchlorosilane.
Trimethylsilanol upon condensation yields a straight chain polymer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\mathrm{Pb}_3 \mathrm{O}_4$ is a mixed oxide of PbO and $\mathrm{PbO}_2$ and reacts with hydrochloric and nitric acid in different ways. Select the correct statement with respect to this difference.
options: $\mathrm{PbO}_2$ does not react with HCl
PbO does not react with $\mathrm{HNO}_3$
$\mathrm{PbO}_2$ does not react with $\mathrm{HNO}_3$
PbO does not react with HCl

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Boron is a fairly rare element. However, it has many important applications. It is a nonmetal and has a very high melting point of $2180^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$. It is extracted from borax and it forms a large number of electron deficient compounds. Choose the correct statement(s).
options: Boron can form $\mathrm{BF}_6^{3-}$ ion.
$\mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ is a basic oxide.
Amorphous boron may be obtained by the reduction of $\mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ at high temperature using sodium or magnesium.
$Crystalline boron may be obtained by thermal decomposition of diborane  \left(\mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{H}_6\right).$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Oxidation of $\mathrm{NaBH}_4$ with iodine results in evolution of a colorless gas, X , along with formation of NaI and hydrogen gas. Three moles of X react with six moles of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ to give an intermediate which upon heating results in Y accompanied by evolution of hydrogen gas. Compounds X and Y , respectively, are
options: $\mathrm{BH}_3, \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{ B} \bullet \mathrm{NH}_3$
$\mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{H}_6, \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{ B} \bullet \mathrm{NH}_3$
$\mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{H}_6, \mathrm{ B}_3 \mathrm{ N}_3 \mathrm{H}_6$
$\mathrm{BH}_3,\left[\mathrm{BH}_2\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{+}\left[\mathrm{BH}_4\right]^{-}$
